text:
deploy-bot: DEPLOY NOTICE: staged rollout started: release/2026-03-15-rc1 -> prod (staged 0.5%). Canary group: service-routing. Rollout ID: rl-2026-0315-07. Observability: p95 lat +4x on routing svc, 502/503 spike from 0.1% -> 2.3% in canary. Auto-pause: disabled. Paging eng-oncall.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: Sev2 - rolling deploy caused increased error rate. Incident channel: #incidents/rl-2026-0315-07. Please ack and follow runbook.

maya: ack. seeing steady 502s for /v1/generate in the canary pool. UX reports timeouts. Can we stop staged traffic and failover to previous routing variant?

aj: on it. Confirming flag key and toggle: `stg.route.v2.enabled`. Will flip to disable now, then trigger traffic rollback.

aj: ```
# disable staged routing (cli)
redwood featureflag disable stg.route.v2.enabled --env prod --rollout rl-2026-0315-07
# then abort the rollout if needed:
redwood deploy abort rl-2026-0315-07 --reason "canary error spike"
```

deploy-bot: Rollout state change: paused by aj at 1867532380. Traffic reroute in progress -> previous routing variant (v1) moved to 100% for service-routing. Canary instances draining.

sylvia: watching metrics: error rate falling rapidly, good. Latency p95 remains ~1.8x vs baseline for a few mins, likely KV cache rewarm + connection priming.

beth: please do not flush global prod caches. We should avoid mass invalidation. Plan: keep failover to v1, allow caches to rewarm, and optionally start a controlled cache-warm on fallback pool (heat-up).

sylvia: agreed. I'll kick a small warm-up job against v1 pool: `k8s run cache-warm --image=tools/cache-warm:latest --replicas=3` in eu-west only.

maya: starting customer impact triage. Which tenants routed through canary in eu-west? Any active SLA customers?

sylvia: pulled audit: AcmeCorp, NovusInc, and LexaHealth had a subset of requests in canary window. Impact likely transient but we should notify account reps. I'll post in #customer-success after this thread.

aj: I submitted `redwood deploy abort rl-2026-0315-07` after bounce checks. Abort confirmed by deploy-bot. Will open post-mortem stub and timeline.

aj: quick status: errors dropping, traffic fully on v1. Canary instances terminated. No rollback of DB or migrations required. No config changes other than feature flag flip.

maya: writing a short outgoing note for affected customers: "We briefly observed elevated errors during a staged routing rollout; we paused and reverted traffic to the prior routing variant. No data loss; service stability restored. We'll follow up with details and mitigations." Sending to SRE/CS for review.

sylvia: taking over incident lead from here for validation and post-rollback checks. I'll watch for error regression and latency normalization for next 2 hours. Handing off: maya -> sylvia.

aj: thanks. I'll update the incident channel and close my on-call loop. sylvia, please escalate to eng-lead if latency doesn't normalize in 30m.

incident-bot: Incident updated: Sev2 ongoing, owner=sylvia, link=https://redwood.internal/incidents/rl-2026-0315-07, runbook=https://redwood.internal/runbooks/deploy-canary.

sylvia: Ack. I'll run health checks and validate API traces, and coordinate with accounts. If we see any recurring 502 patterns on v1, we will open a separate investigation.

maya: noted. Thanks everyone. Leaving notes in the incident timeline and adding the customer-facing blurb.

sylvia: final (for now) — error rate at canary window returned to baseline; latency trending toward normal. Keeping Sev2 open for observation and will update timeline in 30m.
